subject: Security evaluation checklist and DPA / retention clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barker <alex.barker@armourbank.com>, Sara Larkin <sara.larkin@armourbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security evaluation checklist and DPA / retention clarifications

Hi Alex / Sara —

Thanks for the productive demo yesterday. As we discussed, I've pulled together a short checklist to get the security/compliance gating lined up so we can keep the MAP moving toward your target close window (target: early Nov). Attached is a one‑page checklist and a suggested retention matrix for typical telemetry, PII, and customer content.

Key asks from our side to keep the timeline tight:
- Confirm SOC 2 scope you require (Type II preferred; clarify in‑scope services).
- Confirm SIG/CAIQ coverage matrix — we'll complete the CAIQ answers but need to know if you want vendor‑specific evidence for any low‑level controls.
- DPA redlines: please flag any non‑standard clauses up front (subprocessors, cross‑border transfer carveouts, data deletion SLAs).
- Data residency / retention: provide retention windows by data class (transaction logs, customer content, derived embeddings).

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) 2026-09-30 — SIG/CAIQ skeleton and initial SOC 2 statement delivered
2) 2026-10-07 — DPA redlines received from ArmourBank legal
3) 2026-10-14 — Evidence intake / shared drive for artifacts
4) 2026-10-25 — Final signoff on security gates; commercial close to follow

Can you confirm the SOC 2 and residency expectations so we can mark any items that require Private deployment or escrow?

Attachments: ArmourBank_SIG_Initial.xlsx; redwood_retention_matrix.csv

—Michael
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Barker <alex.barker@armourbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Larkin <sara.larkin@armourbank.com>, Legal Ops <legal@armourbank.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security evaluation checklist and DPA / retention clarifications

Michael —

Appreciate the summary and the checklist. Quick answers from our side:
- SOC 2: We require SOC 2 Type II covering the inference runtime and logging/storage for the period of the past 12 months. If you can provide a report + bridge letter where applicable, that should cover our audit needs.
- SIG/CAIQ: We ask for a completed CAIQ and any supporting evidence for network segmentation and key management. I've attached our initial SIG spreadsheet (masked) that highlights must‑have evidence.
- DPA: Primary asks will be around subprocessors disclosures and an explicit clause for EU cross‑border transfers (we may need standard contractual clauses). Data deletion SLA: standard 30/90 windows depending on data class — see below.
- Data residency: For production customer data we prefer EU residency for EU customers; if Redwood needs to provide that, please confirm whether Redwood Private is required or if a hosted EU region is sufficient.

Retention windows (high level):
- Customer content (user prompts/responses): 30 days default, 90 days if agreed in writing
- Derived telemetry/usage: 365 days
- Audit logs/security logs: 7 years (we understand archive/escrow options exist)

We can jump on a 30m call tomorrow to walk through the SIG spreadsheet and DPA redlines.

Attachments: ArmourBank_SIG_Initial.xlsx

—Alex
Alex Barker
Head of Security, ArmourBank

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barker <alex.barker@armourbank.com>, Sara Larkin <sara.larkin@armourbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security evaluation checklist and DPA / retention clarifications

Alex — thanks, that's very helpful. A few clarifications from Redwood's side:

1) SOC 2: We can provide SOC 2 Type II for the inference service and supporting subsystems; our latest report covers through June 2026. We'll include a bridge letter for August–September activity. If you need a tailored scope that excludes Hosted analytics tiers, let us know — we can produce an in‑scope statement.

2) CAIQ/SIG evidence: Kimberly will own the evidence intake; we'll populate the CAIQ and attach network diagrams, KMS architecture diagrams, and our SOC artifact index. For network segmentation we'll include VPC diagrams and ingress/egress rules.

3) DPA redline highlights: we typically accept SCCs for EU transfers and disclose subprocessors on a public registry plus a private list for the contract. Two points to flag:
   - Subprocessors: we can agree to 30-day notice on new subprocessors; for critical subprocessors we can provide 30-day pause for remediation.
   - Data deletion: production content deletion will follow your 30/90 windows; embeddings can be set to 90/365 depending on retention tier.

4) Residency: Hosted EU region is usually sufficient for EU customer data; Private (VPC/on‑prem) is available if you require full physical control or air‑gapped handling. We'll call out any feature parity gaps in the MAP if Private is selected.

I've attached a draft retention matrix (redwood_retention_matrix.csv) that maps data classes and proposed default windows — please flag any discrepancies.

Would middle of next week (2026‑09‑29) for a SIG walkthrough work?

—Michael

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barker <alex.barker@armourbank.com>, Sara Larkin <sara.larkin@armourbank.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security evaluation checklist and DPA / retention clarifications

Hi Alex / Sara —

I'll lead the CAIQ and evidence intake. A few technical points that will help your SIG review team:
- KMS & encryption: Redwood uses customer‑managed keys (optional) and our hosted default KMS for tenant encryption. We can provide key‑rotation cadence and HSM attestations.
- Data deletion pipeline: deletion triggers are applied to active storage immediately and to backups within 30 days; archival buckets can be configured per account for 7+ year retention with documented escrow and retrieval procedures.
- Audit logs: we retain detailed access and system logs for 3 years by default; extended retention to 7 years available via archive.

DPA redline note (attached DPA_redlines_v1.docx):
- We suggested language for subprocessors (30‑day notice + right to pause) and limits on liability tied to agreed SLAs.
- For EU transfers, we propose SCCs + a technical map showing which services touch EU data.

Proposed MAP milestone refinements (technical gating):
A) 2026‑09‑29 — SIG walkthrough (30m) + evidence list published
B) 2026‑10‑05 — DPA redlines exchanged (legal review)
C) 2026‑10‑12 — Evidence intake complete (artifact links in Drive)
D) 2026‑10‑20 — Final security gate signoff

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v1.docx

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Larkin <sara.larkin@armourbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Alex Barker <alex.barker@armourbank.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@armourbank.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security evaluation checklist and DPA / retention clarifications

Thanks everyone — that reads well and helps us align internally. Quick notes and next steps from ArmourBank: 
1) SIG walkthrough accepted for 2026-09-29 at 10:00am PT — please send an invite.
2) We'll have legal push DPA redlines by 2026‑10‑04; we'll mark any non‑negotiables (SCCs/subprocessors) in red.
3) Retention: we agree to the proposed defaults but will confirm a small set of accounts that require extended 7‑year archival (we'll provide a list by 10/05).
4) Escrow: please provide your standard archive/escrow SOP and pricing if we elect the extended archival lane.

Action items: 
- Michael: send SIG walkthrough invite and Team Drive link for artifacts.
- Kimberly: publish CAIQ + evidence checklist to the shared Drive.
- Alex / Legal: deliver DPA redlines by 10/04.

Once DPA redlines are in and SIG evidence is uploaded we'll move the security gate to "review complete" and proceed to commercial close steps. Thanks for the clear MAP — looking forward to the walkthrough.

—Sara Larkin
Head of Risk & Compliance, ArmourBank
